claim: The XLFM can image sparse neural activity over the larval zebrafish brain at near single cell resolution and at a volume rate of 77 Hz.
source: The XLFM can image sparse neural activity over the larval zebrafish brain at near single cell resolution and at a volume rate of 77 Hz, with the aid of genetically encoded calcium indicator GCamp6f.
evidence: The manuscript directly states the imaging capabilities of XLFM including resolution and speed.

claim: Larval zebrafish can move at an instantaneous velocity up to 50 mm/s.
source: They can move at an instantaneous velocity up to 50 mm/s (Severi et al., 2014) and acceleration of 1 g (9.83 m/s2).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Severi et al., 2014.

claim: Larval zebrafish can move with acceleration of 1 g (9.83 m/s2).
source: They can move at an instantaneous velocity up to 50 mm/s (Severi et al., 2014) and acceleration of 1 g (9.83 m/s2).
evidence: The manuscript directly states the acceleration capability of larval zebrafish.

claim: The implementation of flashed fluorescence excitation (200 μs in duration) allowed blur-free fluorescent images to be captured when a zebrafish moved at a speed up to 10 mm/s.
source: Furthermore, the implementation of flashed fluorescence excitation (200 μs in duration) allowed blur-free fluorescent images to be captured when a zebrafish moved at a speed up to 10 mm/s.
evidence: The manuscript directly states the technical capability of the flashed excitation method.

claim: Larval zebrafish are an attractive model system to investigate the neural correlates of behaviors owing to their small brain size, optical transparency, and rich behavioral repertoire.
source: Larval zebrafish (Danio rerio) are an attractive model system to investigate the neural correlates of behaviors owing to their small brain size, optical transparency, and rich behavioral repertoire (Friedrich et al., 2010; Ahrens and Engert, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Friedrich et al., 2010 and Ahrens and Engert, 2015.

claim: The total number of neurons in a larval zebrafish brain is approximately 80,000.
source: Given the total number of neurons (~80,000 [Hill et al., 2003]) in a larval zebrafish brain, we next introduced a sparseness index ρ, defined as the fraction of neurons in the brain active at a given instant, and used numerical simulation and our reconstruction algorithm to characterize the dependence of achievable resolution on ρ.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hill et al., 2003.

claim: A critical sparseness index ρc ≈ 0.11 was identified, below which active neurons could be resolved at the optimal resolution.
source: We identified a critical ρc ≈ 0.11, below which active neurons could be resolved at the optimal resolution (Figure 1—figure supplement 11b).
evidence: The claim is supported by numerical simulation data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 11b.

claim: The fluorescent intensity loss due to photobleaching reached ~50% when the zebrafish was imaged continuously for ~100 min and over more than 300,000 volumes.
source: The fluorescent intensity loss due to photobleaching reached ~50% when the zebrafish, which expressed pan-neuronal nucleus-labelled GCamp6f (huc:h2b-gcamp6f), was imaged continuously for ~100 min and over more than 300,000 volumes (Figure 1—figure supplement 12, Video 2 and 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 12.

claim: Different groups of neurons in the forebrain, midbrain, and hindbrain were activated at different times during visual stimulation.
source: We found that different groups of neurons in the forebrain, midbrain, and hindbrain were activated at different times (Figure 1e–f, Video 1 and 4), suggesting rapid sensorimotor transformation across different brain regions.
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1e-f and Videos 1 and 4.

claim: The XLFM had ~ Ø800 μm in plane coverage and more than 400 μm depth of view.
source: In our design, the system had ~ Ø800 μm in plane coverage (Ø is the diameter of the lateral field of view) and more than 400 μm depth of view, within which an optimal resolution of 3.4 μm × 3.4 μm × 5 μm could be achieved over a depth of 200 μm (Figure 1—figure supplements 6 and 7, Materials and methods).
evidence: The claim is supported by characterization data in Figure 1—figure supplements 6 and 7.

claim: An optimal resolution of 3.4 μm × 3.4 μm × 5 μm could be achieved over a depth of 200 μm.
source: In our design, the system had ~ Ø800 μm in plane coverage (Ø is the diameter of the lateral field of view) and more than 400 μm depth of view, within which an optimal resolution of 3.4 μm × 3.4 μm × 5 μm could be achieved over a depth of 200 μm (Figure 1—figure supplements 6 and 7, Materials and methods).
evidence: The claim is supported by characterization data in Figure 1—figure supplements 6 and 7.

claim: The imaging performance suffered from the variation in the focal length of the micro-lenses.
source: In the current implementation, however, the imaging performance suffered from the variation in the focal length of the micro-lenses (Figure 1—figure supplement 8), which led to spatial variance of the PSF.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 8.

claim: The reconstruction performance and the achievable optimal resolution were shown to degrade beyond the volume of Ø500 μm × 100 μm.
source: As a result, the reconstruction performance and the achievable optimal resolution were shown to degrade beyond the volume of Ø500 μm × 100 μm (Figure 1—figure supplements 9 and 10).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplements 9 and 10.

claim: All imaging reconstructions were carried out over a volume of Ø800 μm × 400 μm to minimize the reconstruction time while assuring whole brain coverage.
source: To minimize the reconstruction time while assuring whole brain coverage (~250 μm thick), all imaging reconstructions were carried out over a volume of Ø800 μm × 400 μm.
evidence: The manuscript directly states the reconstruction volume used.

claim: The customized lenslet array was placed at the rear pupil plane of the imaging objective.
source: First, a customized lenslet array (Figure 1a, Figure 1—figure supplement 1) was placed at the rear pupil plane of the imaging objective, instead of at the imaging plane as in LFM.
evidence: The manuscript directly describes the optical configuration shown in Figure 1a.

claim: In ideal conditions, a 2D spatially invariant point spread function (PSF) could be defined and measured in XLFM.
source: Therefore, in ideal conditions, a 2D spatially invariant point spread function (PSF) could be defined and measured; in practice, the PSF was approximately spatially invariant (see Materials and methods).
evidence: The manuscript directly states the theoretical property of the PSF in XLFM.

claim: Multifocal imaging was introduced to further increase the depth of view by dividing the micro-lenses array into two groups whose focal planes were at different axial positions.
source: Third, multifocal imaging (Abrahamsson et al., 2013; Perwass and Wietzke, 2012) was introduced to further increase the depth of view by dividing the micro-lenses array into two groups whose focal planes were at different axial positions (Figure 1b and c, Figure 1—figure supplements 3 and 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations and illustrated in Figures 1b, 1c, and supplements 3 and 4.

claim: A new computational algorithm based on optical wave theory was developed to reconstruct the entire 3D volume from one image.
source: Fourth, a new computational algorithm based on optical wave theory was developed to reconstruct the entire 3D volume from one image (Figure 1—figure supplement 5) captured by a fast camera (see Materials and methods).
evidence: The manuscript directly states the development of a new algorithm.

claim: The tracking system compensated for fish movement by continuously adjusting the lateral positions of the motorized stage at 300 Hz.
source: Tracking and autofocusing allowed for rapid compensation of 3D fish movement (300 Hz in x and y, 100 Hz in z, Figure 3a) and retainment of the fish head within the field of view of the imaging objective.
evidence: The manuscript directly states the tracking speed and references Figure 3a.

claim: The autofocus system compensated for axial fish movement at 100 Hz.
source: Tracking and autofocusing allowed for rapid compensation of 3D fish movement (300 Hz in x and y, 100 Hz in z, Figure 3a) and retainment of the fish head within the field of view of the imaging objective.
evidence: The manuscript directly states the autofocus speed and references Figure 3a.

claim: Eyes converged rapidly when the fish entered the prey capture state.
source: Consistent with several earlier findings (Bianco et al., 2011; Patterson et al., 2013; Trivedi and Bollmann, 2013), eyes converged rapidly when the fish entered the prey capture state (Figure 3c).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations and data shown in Figure 3c.

claim: When a paramecium moved into the visual field of the fish, groups of neurons near the contralateral optical tectum of the fish were first activated.
source: When a paramecium moved into the visual field of the fish, groups of neurons, indicated as group one in Figure 4b, near the contralateral optical tectum of the fish were first activated (t1).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: The earliest tectal activity (group 1) is responsible for prey detection.
source: The earliest tectal activity (group 1) responsible for prey detection found here is consistent with previous studies (Semmelhack et al., 2014; Bianco and Engert, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Semmelhack et al., 2014 and Bianco and Engert, 2015.

claim: Whole brain imaging in freely behaving animals has been previously reported in Caenorhabditis elegans.
source: Whole brain imaging in freely behaving animals has been previously reported in Caenorhabditis elegans, by integrating spinning-disk confocal microscopy with a 2D tracking system (Venkatachalam et al., 2016; Nguyen et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Venkatachalam et al., 2016 and Nguyen et al., 2016.

claim: Howard Berg pioneered the use of 3D tracking microscopy to study bacteria chemotaxis.
source: In the more remote past, Howard Berg pioneered the use of 3D tracking microscopy to study bacteria chemotaxis (Berg, 1971).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Berg, 1971.

claim: The XLFM overcomes several critical limitations of conventional LFM and allows optimization of imaging volume, resolution, and speed simultaneously.
source: The XLFM, derived from the general concept of light field imaging (Broxton et al., 2013; Adelson and Wang, 1992; Ng et al., 2005; Levoy et al., 2006), overcomes several critical limitations of conventional LFM and allows optimization of imaging volume, resolution, and speed simultaneously.
evidence: The manuscript directly states the advantages of XLFM over conventional LFM, with supporting citations.

claim: XLFM can be perfectly combined with flashed fluorescence excitation to capture blur-free images at high resolution during rapid fish movement.
source: Furthermore, it can be perfectly combined with flashed fluorescence excitation to capture blur-free images at high resolution during rapid fish movement.
evidence: The manuscript directly states this capability of XLFM.

claim: Sensory information processing depends strongly on the locomotor state of an animal.
source: A large body of research suggests that sensory information processing depends strongly on the locomotor state of an animal (Niell and Stryker, 2010; Maimon et al., 2010; Chiappe et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Niell and Stryker, 2010; Maimon et al., 2010; and Chiappe et al., 2010.

claim: The ability to sense self-motion, such as proprioceptive feedback and efferent copy, can profoundly shape the dynamics of the neural circuit and perception.
source: The ability to sense self-motion, such as proprioceptive feedback (Pearson, 1995) and efferent copy (Bell, 1981), can also profoundly shape the dynamics of the neural circuit and perception.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Pearson, 1995 and Bell, 1981.

claim: Population neuronal activities are sparse.
source: A growing body of experimental data indeed suggests that population neuronal activities are sparse (Hromádka et al., 2008; Buzsáki and Mizuseki, 2014) and sparse representation is useful for efficient neural computation (Olshausen and Field, 1996; Olshausen and Field, 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Hromádka et al., 2008 and Buzsáki and Mizuseki, 2014.

claim: Sparse representation is useful for efficient neural computation.
source: A growing body of experimental data indeed suggests that population neuronal activities are sparse (Hromádka et al., 2008; Buzsáki and Mizuseki, 2014) and sparse representation is useful for efficient neural computation (Olshausen and Field, 1996; Olshausen and Field, 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Olshausen and Field, 1996 and Olshausen and Field, 2004.

claim: When the fraction of active neurons in a given imaging frame was less than ρc ≈ 0.11, individual neurons could be resolved at optimal resolution.
source: Given the total number of neurons in the larval zebrafish brain, we found that when the fraction of active neurons in a given imaging frame was less than ρc ≈ 0.11, individual neurons could be resolved at optimal resolution.
evidence: The manuscript directly states this finding from numerical simulations.

claim: When population neural activity was dense, a coarse-grained neural activity map with reduced resolution was obtained.
source: When population neural activity was dense (e.g., neurons have high firing rate and firing patterns have large spatiotemporal correlation), we obtained a coarse-grained neural activity map with reduced resolution.
evidence: The manuscript directly states this limitation of the system.

claim: The linear acceleration of the swimming fish, encoded by vestibular feedback, was significantly underestimated due to motion compensation by the tracking system.
source: The linear acceleration of the swimming fish, encoded by vestibular feedback, was significantly underestimated.
evidence: The manuscript directly states this limitation of the tracking approach.

claim: The perception of angular acceleration during head orientation remained largely intact in the tracking system.
source: The perception of angular acceleration during head orientation remained largely intact.
evidence: The manuscript directly states this aspect of the tracking system.

claim: The relative flow velocity along the fish body was invariant upon stage translation and can still be detected by specific hair cells in the lateral line system.
source: The relative flow velocity along the fish body, which was invariant upon stage translation, can still be detected by specific hair cells in the lateral line system (Coombs, 2014; Liao, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Coombs, 2014 and Liao, 2010.

claim: The current axial displacement employed by the piezo scanner had a limited travelling range (400 µm).
source: For example, the current axial displacement employed by the piezo scanner had a limited travelling range (400 µm), and our swimming chamber essentially restrained the movement of the zebrafish in two dimensions.
evidence: The manuscript directly states this technical limitation.

claim: The swimming chamber essentially restrained the movement of the zebrafish in two dimensions.
source: For example, the current axial displacement employed by the piezo scanner had a limited travelling range (400 µm), and our swimming chamber essentially restrained the movement of the zebrafish in two dimensions.
evidence: The manuscript directly states this limitation of the experimental setup.

claim: The performance degradation caused by focal length variation of the micro-lenses could be resolved by higher precision machining.
source: In XLFM, the performance degradation caused by focal length variation of the micro-lenses could be resolved by higher precision machining.
evidence: The manuscript directly states this potential improvement.

claim: With more pixels on the imaging sensor, more densely labelled samples could be resolved.
source: With more pixels on the imaging sensor, we could resolve more densely labelled samples, and achieve higher spatial resolution without sacrificing imaging volume coverage by introducing more than two different focal planes formed by more groups of micro-lenses.
evidence: The manuscript directly states this potential improvement.

claim: The fast imaging speed of XLFM holds the potential for recording electrical activity when high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) fluorescent voltage sensors become available.
source: Additionally, the fast imaging speed of XLFM holds the potential for recording electrical activity when high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) fluorescent voltage sensors become available (St-Pierre et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to St-Pierre et al., 2014.

claim: The illumination-independent characteristic of XLFM is perfectly suitable for recording brain activities from bioluminescent calcium/voltage indicators in a truly natural environment.
source: Finally, the illumination-independent characteristic of XLFM is perfectly suitable for recording brain activities from bioluminescent calcium/voltage indicators in a truly natural environment, where light interference arising from fluorescence excitation can be eliminated (Naumann et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Naumann et al., 2010.

claim: Light sheet microscopy has demonstrated entire brain coverage and single neuron resolution in restrained zebrafish.
source: While light sheet microscopy (LSM) has demonstrated entire brain coverage and single neuron resolution in restrained zebrafish (Ahrens et al., 2013), it lacks the speed to follow rapid fish movement.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Ahrens et al., 2013.

claim: Light sheet microscopy lacks the speed to follow rapid fish movement.
source: While light sheet microscopy (LSM) has demonstrated entire brain coverage and single neuron resolution in restrained zebrafish (Ahrens et al., 2013), it lacks the speed to follow rapid fish movement.
evidence: The manuscript directly states this limitation of LSM.

claim: In light sheet microscopy, the sample is illuminated from its side, a configuration that is difficult to be integrated with a tracking system.
source: Moreover, in LSM, the sample is illuminated from its side, a configuration that is difficult to be integrated with a tracking system.
evidence: The manuscript directly states this limitation of LSM.

claim: Conventional light field microscopy has relatively low spatial resolution.
source: Conventional light field microscopy (LFM) (Broxton et al., 2013; Prevedel et al., 2014) is a promising alternative due to its higher imaging speed; however, its spatial resolution is relatively low.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Broxton et al., 2013 and Prevedel et al., 2014.

claim: Specialized LFMs for monitoring neural activity utilizing temporal information rely on spatiotemporal sparsity of fluorescent signals and cannot be applied to moving animals.
source: Specialized LFMs for monitoring neural activity utilizing temporal information were also developed recently (Pégard et al., 2016; Nöbauer et al., 2017), which rely on spatiotemporal sparsity of fluorescent signals and cannot be applied to moving animals.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Pégard et al., 2016 and Nöbauer et al., 2017.

claim: Vestibular as well as proprioceptive feedbacks are likely perturbed in immobilized zebrafish.
source: For example, it is likely that vestibular as well as proprioceptive feedbacks are perturbed in immobilized zebrafish (Engert, 2012; Bianco et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Engert, 2012 and Bianco et al., 2012.

claim: The crowning moment during hunting behavior when a fish succeeds in catching a paramecium cannot be easily replicated in a virtual reality setting.
source: The crowning moment during hunting behavior (Bianco et al., 2011; Patterson et al., 2013; Trivedi and Bollmann, 2013) — when a fish succeeds in catching a paramecium — cannot be easily replicated in a virtual reality setting.
evidence: The manuscript directly states this limitation of virtual reality approaches, with supporting citations.

claim: Current studies on freely swimming zebrafish are either limited to non-imaging optical systems or wide field imaging at low resolution.
source: Current studies on freely swimming zebrafish are either limited to non-imaging optical systems (Naumann et al., 2010) or wide field imaging at low resolution (Muto et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Naumann et al., 2010 and Muto et al., 2013.

claim: The imaging system was a customized upright microscope.
source: The imaging system (Figure 1) was a customized upright microscope.
evidence: The manuscript directly describes the imaging system.

claim: A blue laser (Coherent, OBIS 488 nm, 100 mW, USA) was used for fluorescence excitation.
source: Along the fluorescence excitation light path, a blue laser (Coherent, OBIS 488 nm, 100 mW, USA) was expanded and collimated into a beam with a diameter of ~25 mm.
evidence: The manuscript directly describes the excitation laser used.

claim: The total magnification of the imaging system was ~4.
source: The total magnification of the imaging system was ~4, so one camera pixel (6.5 µm) corresponded to ~1.6 µm on the sample.
evidence: The manuscript directly states the magnification of the system.

claim: One camera pixel (6.5 µm) corresponded to ~1.6 µm on the sample.
source: The total magnification of the imaging system was ~4, so one camera pixel (6.5 µm) corresponded to ~1.6 µm on the sample.
evidence: The manuscript directly states the pixel-to-sample correspondence.

claim: Due to the blockage of light by the aluminum micro-lenses housing, 16% of the light after a 1.05 NA imaging objective was effectively collected by the camera.
source: Due to the blockage of light by the aluminum micro-lenses housing, 16% of the light after a 1.05 NA imaging objective was effectively collected by the camera.
evidence: The manuscript directly states the light collection efficiency.

claim: The light collection efficiency of 16% is equivalent to using a 0.4 NA imaging objective.
source: This efficiency is equivalent to using a 0.4 NA imaging objective.
evidence: The manuscript directly states this equivalence.

claim: It took about 4 min to reconstruct one 3D volume using a desktop computer with a GPU (Nvidia Titan X).
source: It took about 4 min to reconstruct one 3D volume using a desktop computer with a GPU (Nvidia Titan X).
evidence: The manuscript directly states the reconstruction time.

claim: The reconstruction ran ~20 × slower using a CPU (Intel E5-2630v2) compared to GPU.
source: In comparison, the reconstruction ran ~20 × slower using a CPU (Intel E5-2630v2) on a Dell desktop.
evidence: The manuscript directly states the speed comparison.

claim: The optical transfer function (OTF) was extended to a spatial frequency of ~1/3.4 µm−1.
source: The optical transfer function (OTF), which is the Fourier transform of the PSF in the x-y plane, was extended to a spatial frequency of ~1/3.4 µm−1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 6), a result that agreed well with the designed resolution at 3.4 μm, given that the equivalent NA of individual micro-lenses was 0.075.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 6.

claim: The equivalent NA of individual micro-lenses was 0.075.
source: The optical transfer function (OTF), which is the Fourier transform of the PSF in the x-y plane, was extended to a spatial frequency of ~1/3.4 µm−1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 6), a result that agreed well with the designed resolution at 3.4 μm, given that the equivalent NA of individual micro-lenses was 0.075.
evidence: The manuscript directly states the equivalent NA.

claim: The lateral resolution was preserved across the designed cylindrical imaging volume of Ø800 μm × 200 μm when measured from the raw PSF behind individual micro-lenses.
source: The lateral resolution, measured from the raw PSF behind individual micro-lenses, was preserved across the designed cylindrical imaging volume of Ø800 μm × 200 μm (Figure 1—figure supplement 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 6.

claim: The designed lateral resolution of 3.4 µm could be preserved over a volume of Ø800 μm × 200 μm by reducing focal length variation to below 0.3%.
source: In principle, the designed lateral resolution of 3.4 µm could be preserved over a volume of Ø800 μm × 200 μm by reducing focal length variation to below 0.3%
evidence: The manuscript directly states this potential improvement.

claim: The optimal axial resolution at 5 µm could be achieved over an axial coverage of 200 μm by minimizing micro-lens focal length variation.
source: We believe that the optimal axial resolution at 5 µm could be achieved over an axial coverage of 200 μm by minimizing micro-lens focal length variation (Figure 1—figure supplement 8).
evidence: The manuscript directly states this potential improvement.

claim: Each active neuron was assumed to emit 20,000 photons in the numerical simulations.
source: In all calculations, the Poisson noise was properly considered by assuming that each active neuron emitted 20,000 photons, 2.2% of which were collected by our imaging system.
evidence: The manuscript directly states the simulation parameters.

claim: 2.2% of emitted photons were collected by the imaging system.
source: In all calculations, the Poisson noise was properly considered by assuming that each active neuron emitted 20,000 photons, 2.2% of which were collected by our imaging system.
evidence: The manuscript directly states the collection efficiency.

claim: The rate-limiting factor of the lateral tracking system was the response time of the stage (~300 Hz).
source: The rate-limiting factor of our lateral tracking system was the response time of the stage (~300 Hz).
evidence: The manuscript directly states the rate-limiting factor.

claim: The closed loop delay of the autofocus system was ~5 ms.
source: The feedback control system was written in LabVIEW. The code was further accelerated by parallel processing and the closed loop delay was ~5 ms.
evidence: The manuscript directly states the closed loop delay.

claim: The rate-limiting factor of the autofocus system was the settling time of the piezo scanner, which was about 10 ms.
source: The rate-limiting factor of the autofocus system was the settling time of the piezo scanner (PI P725KHDS, Germany, 400 μm travelling distance), which was about 10 ms.
evidence: The manuscript directly states the rate-limiting factor.

claim: The high magnification real-time analysis was run at ~120 fps.
source: The high mag RT analysis was run at ~120 fps and the low mag RT analysis was run at ~180 fps.
evidence: The manuscript directly states the analysis speed.

claim: The low magnification real-time analysis was run at ~180 fps.
source: The high mag RT analysis was run at ~120 fps and the low mag RT analysis was run at ~180 fps.
evidence: The manuscript directly states the analysis speed.

claim: All larval zebrafish were raised in embryo medium under 28.5°C and a 14/10 hr light/dark cycle.
source: All larval zebrafish (huc:h2b-gcamp6f and huc:gcamp6s) were raised in embryo medium under 28.5°C and a 14/10 hr light/dark cycle.
evidence: The manuscript directly describes the animal husbandry conditions.

claim: Zebrafish were fed with paramecium from 4 dpf.
source: Zebrafish were fed with paramecium from 4 dpf.
evidence: The manuscript directly describes the feeding protocol.

source: For restrained experiments, 4–6 dpf zebrafish were embedded in 1% low melting point agarose.
evidence: The manuscript directly describes the experimental protocol.

claim: For freely moving experiments, 7–11 dpf zebrafish were used.
source: For freely moving experiments, 7–11 dpf zebrafish with 10% Hank's solution were transferred to a customized chamber (20 mm in diameter, 0.8 mm in depth), and 10–20 paramecia were added before the chamber was covered by a coverslip.

claim: Each experiment was repeated at least three times with similar experimental conditions.
source: Each experiment was repeated at least three times with similar experimental conditions.
